steps.title: Variable
steps.body: A named storage location in memory whose value can change during program execution. Constant: A named value that cannot be changed once it has been set.

steps.title: Assignment
steps.body: means storing a value in a variable. The variable name goes on the left, the value or expression goes on the right. The previous value is overwritten.

steps.title: Sequence
steps.body: means executing instructions one after another in order, from top to bottom. This is the simplest programming construct - every program uses sequence.

steps.title: Selection
steps.body: allows a program to choose between different paths based on a condition. The three forms are: IF...THEN, IF...THEN...ELSE, and CASE/SWITCH.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain the difference between a variable and a constant. | Write pseudo-code that asks for a number and outputs "Positive", "Negative", or "Zero" using selection. | When would you use a REPEAT...UNTIL loop instead of a WHILE loop?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A variable is a named memory location whose value can change during execution. A constant is a named value that cannot be changed once set. Constants prevent accidental changes and make code more read | INPUT number IF number > 0 THEN OUTPUT "Positive" ELSEIF number < 0 THEN OUTPUT "Negative" ELSE OUTPUT "Zero" ENDIF | Use REPEAT...UNTIL when the loop body must execute at least once (e.g. input validation). Use WHILE when the loop may need to execute zero times (e.g. searching a list that might be empty).

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always close your constructs: ENDIF, ENDWHILE, NEXT, ENDCASE Use constants (CONST) for values that should never change Choose the right loop: FOR for counted, WHILE for pre-condition, REPEAT for post-condition WHILE checks before running; REPEAT checks after - know the difference Indent nested constructs to show structure clearly Remember: sequence, selection, and iteration are the THREE basic constructs
